title: decade's own chrome builds without smithay
body:
The remote viewer in decade-e3a784 draws decade's chrome itself, and on macOS it has no smithay. The chrome it needs is decade's own, all in `decade/src/server/chrome/`: `Frame` in `frame.rs` (top bar, sidebar, agent cards), the palette `Menu`, `Picker`, the settings `Panel` and `Settings`. Only `picker.rs` imports smithay, for `Point`, `Rectangle` and `Size` as plain geometry. smithay is a Linux-only dependency in `decade/Cargo.toml`. The widgets sit under `server`, and some import from it: `menu.rs` takes `apps::App`, and `picker.rs` takes `workspace::Workspace`.

## Proposal

These widgets move to a module outside `server` that imports nothing from smithay or `crate::server`, and they use `decade-ui`'s types. The data they draw from comes in as plain values, in the shape the remote viewer will receive from the server. A macOS build of the viewer compiles the module and leaves out the server.

## Open

- What `Picker` shows for workspace thumbnails when the compositor that renders them runs on another machine.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/8a3a6cd2
notes.text:
The new `chrome` module names no smithay and no `crate::server`, but it is not yet compiled for any target besides Linux. `main.rs` declares it as `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")] mod chrome;`, like its siblings. `settings.rs` uses `crate::files`, which is declared the same way, although its contents are portable std code. A macOS viewer has to lift both gates, and nothing has checked the module on another target.

On the open question: the picker only lays out a `Grid` of thumbnail rectangles. `paint_picker` in `server/compositor/render.rs` paints each workspace into its rectangle, so a remote viewer paints whatever the server sends for a thumbnail.
